newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET - Test recall not enough for Pocock.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Test recall not enough for Pocock.

text.p: TAURANGA, Jan 17 - Earning a well-deserved recall to the New Zealand cricket team for next week's test against England isn't even half the battle for rejuvenated Northern Districts captain Blair Pocock, NZPA reports.
Cementing his place at the top of New Zealand's batting order has now got to be the priority, Pocock said on Friday from his Auckland home.
"I'm delighted to be back -- playing for their country is why every first-class cricketer plays the game -- but I've now got to get out there and score some runs," he said.
"The team, from what I understand, have only been picked for the one game and to put it very simply, if I don't score runs I don't expect to get picked for the next game."
Pocock's recall yesterday to partner ND team-mate Bryan Young at the top of the New Zealand innings is another cog in the 25-year-old's injury-plagued cricket career.
First picked in 1993, Pocock was invalided home from the tour of England the following year with a shoulder injury.

After two operations, Pocock again found favour with the national selectors five months ago when he was not only picked in the team to tour Sharjah and Pakistan but was one of a dozen players given New Zealand contracts.
But the shoulder injury flared again, preventing Pocock from touring, and his place was taken by Young, who grabbed his chance and established himself as the leading opener.
Pocock said he was obviously disappointed to miss last year's tour but was happy the selectors deemed his form good enough to add to his six tests.

"I don't think my form has been so conclusive that I was an automatic selection. There's a lot of other good openers around who've been scoring runs but I'm happy that it's me who's been given the opportunity."

After playing in the NZ Selection 11 which were routed by England in Palmerston North this week, Pocock gets another opportunity to view their attack when ND play the tourists in Hamilton starting tomorrow.
They were a team, he said, who possessed a good bowling attack and his big goal in leading ND into the first-class fixture was that the home side was competitive.
ND coach Chris Kuggeleijn has similar goals, although he admitted after the "razamatazz" of the Shell Cup one-day competition, they hadn't really focused on the clash.
"I'll make sure the boys become focused when we get together in the nets this afternoon and I'm sure it's a game they've been looking forward to all season.
"It isn't every day you get to play an international side and I hope we do a lot better than the last team to come up against them."

Thames Valley seamer Dion Bennett looks set to make his first-class debut for ND tomorrow after his good form for the second 11 earned him a call-up into the 12-man squad picked for the four-day game.

Kuggeleijn was giving nothing away today about his likely selection after New Zealand coach Steve Rixon called for Simon Doull to be rested from the game but he did say a four-pronged seam attack was a possibility if the pitch had the expected pace and bounce.

The Northern Districts team with 12th man still to be decided is: Blair Pocock (captain), Mark Bailey, Matthew Bell, Dion Bennett, Simon Doull, Matthew Hart, Robert Hart, Michael Parlane, Scott Styris, Alex Tait, Daniel Vettori, Bryan Young.
